Release notes/v0.7.2/Oct 19, 2026

What's new in Cadence 0.7.2.

Cadence now arranges your windows. Start with your command word and say where things go: "computer, tile my terminals on my larger monitor", "computer, Chrome on the left and Slack on the right", "computer, undo that".

By Cadence Labs · Filed in Releases

§01 New

  • Window management by voice. Any app's windows, on any of your displays:
    • Parts of a screen: halves, thirds, two thirds, quarters, three quarters, corners, sixths, "the left 60 percent", center, maximize.
    • Several windows at once: "Chrome on the left, Slack on the right", "VS Code on the left two thirds and my terminals stacked on the right", "Chrome on the left and everything else on the right". A side fits around what the other windows take.
    • Layouts: side by side, columns, rows, a grid, ratios like 70/30 or two thirds and one third, one main window with the rest stacked beside it, a cascade, or spread across all your monitors.
    • Displays: "move this to my other monitor", "put Slack on my laptop", "bring all my windows to this screen".
    • One window at a time: "make this a bit bigger", "make it wider", "swap Chrome and Slack", "minimize everything except Chrome", "hide others", "bring back Slack".
    • Saved layouts: "save this layout as coding", then "open my coding layout". Each window comes back to the same part of its display, even after you plug in a different monitor.
    • Undo: "undo that" steps back through your last 20 window changes, and "redo" steps forward again.
  • Said your way. The usual phrasings are understood on your Mac and move windows right away. Anything else about windows goes to Claude Haiku on your own Claude Code login, which sees your window titles, so "give the docs window most of the big screen" works too. The toolbar shows Arranging… while it works it out. Every example is in Settings → Commands → Windows.
